subject: FreshCart renewal: ops plan, tier rebalance and monthly commit uplift
messages:
From: Maria Alvarez <maria@freshcart.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.example>
Cc: Pedro Soto <pedro@freshcart.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: FreshCart renewal planning + burst/commit questions

Hi Irene —

We’re kicking off our renewal planning and would like to explore increasing our Hosted API monthly commit for the next 12 months. Current plan: 50M tokens/month. Traffic projections for Black November + holiday promo indicate a need for ~150M tokens/month (peak expected Nov–Dec).

Key asks:
- Can Redwood support a step-up commit that ramps (50 -> 100 -> 150M) across the next 3 months?
- What happens to rate limits and soft throttle thresholds with a higher commit? We have some latency-sensitive endpoints and want to avoid degraded SLOs.
- Any paperwork/PO cadence we should prepare for?

I attached a short telemetry extract (Q2 usage) to help sizing. Also happy to do a 30-min ops call this week.

Thanks,
Maria
Head of Platform
FreshCart

Attachment: FreshCart_usage_2028Q2.csv (csv)

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.example>
To: Maria Alvarez <maria@freshcart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.example>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.example>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FreshCart renewal planning + burst/commit questions

Hi Maria —

Thanks for the context and the usage file — that helped. Short answers up front: yes, we can support a stepped monthly commit (50 -> 100 -> 150M) and we have a recommended ops plan to preserve latency SLOs while increasing throughput.

Proposed operational approach:
1) Ramp windows: 30-day step windows (start 1st of month). We’ll reserve headroom at each step for burst pockets.
2) Canary routing: route 5–10% traffic to the new commit pool for the first 72 hours after each step to monitor KV cache hit rates and tail latency.
3) Soft throttle mapping: we’ll map your current per-route rate limits to scaled thresholds; we recommend keeping latency-sensitive endpoints on the low-latency routing tier.
4) Billing & paperwork: we can do an amendment + PO. Karthik will draft pricing tiers and a one-page amendment for signature.

Can you confirm the desired calendar for the step-up (which month to start the first move) and whether you need Dedicated capacity on specific regions?

I’ll schedule a 30-min ops sync for Thursday; Karthik and Vanessa will join.

Best,
Irene
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.example>
To: Maria Alvarez <maria@freshcart.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.example>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 26 Jul 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: FreshCart renewal planning + tier mapping

Hi Maria — quick note on pricing/limits to set expectations before our call.

Illustrative pricing (monthly commit):
- 50M tokens: baseline (current) — existing rateband applies.
- 100M tokens: baseline price less 7% unit discount + standard burst pocket (10% monthly).
- 150M tokens: additional 10% unit discount on the incremental volume above 100M + optional reserved burst (15%).

Rate-limit and throttle behavior:
- Per-route qps caps will scale roughly linearly with commit increases; however, sustained per-route qps above the low-latency tier may be routed to a cost-optimized tier (higher latency but cheaper).
- Soft throttle triggers (75/90/95 percentiles) will be recalculated using your historical tail latency; we’ll share a suggested config in the amendment.

Operational asks from FreshCart for a smooth rollout:
- A canonical list of latency-sensitive endpoints (path + SLA target).
- A brief spike playbook (who to call, escalation matrix).

I attached a draft amendment (docx) and a short rate mapping table. Irene — can you attach the DocuSign link after legal review?

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Renewal_Amendment_FreshCart_v1.docx (docx)
